A1.justification: Both 38-page PDFs describe the same WanderDream work and include Appendices A–F. Text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison despite changed margins and early-page reflow.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original video-generation, situated-QA, and real-world transfer experiments. Appendix C also reports comparisons between automated judges and human evaluations.

after.justification: The original experiments remain in Section 5 and Appendix C, including world-model evaluations, real-world transfer results, and human–judge agreement.

M1.justification: The data-generation procedures, sequential imagination-and-reasoning frameworks, and panoramic adaptation of MindJourney are unchanged. Appendix Algorithms 1–2 retain the same steps.

E1.justification: Both versions use HM3D, ScanNet++, and the same office/apartment real-world test set for video generation and situated QA. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The world-model and MLLM comparator sets in Tables 3–6 and Figure 7 are unchanged, including MindJourney in the real-world comparison. Table 9 retains the same judge and prompt-template comparisons.

E3.justification: Dataset splits, frame sampling, resolutions, training budgets, and evaluation metrics remain unchanged in Sections 3–5 and the appendices. Table 8 retains the same fine-tuning settings.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the frame-input analysis in Figure 7, judge/template ablations in Table 9, failure cases in Figure 9, and qualitative comparisons in Appendix D and Figures 23–24.

E5.justification: The ± reporting in Tables 2, 3, and 6 and the human-evaluation information are unchanged. No seed, repeated-run, confidence-interval, or significance-testing information is added or removed.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 6 retains QA scores of 43.0 for Wan2.1 with LoRA and 31.9 for MindJourney; the qualitative figure images also match.

T1.justification: The shortest-path assumptions and scoring equation (1) are unchanged. No mathematical definition, derivation, theorem, or proof is added, removed, or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same dataset contributions and claims about imagination supporting situated reasoning and sim-to-real transfer.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning contextual interference, generation quality, and transferability remain unchanged. Section 6 and Appendix E retain the same failure explanations, latency limitations, and future-work boundaries.

D1.justification: The abstract adds the RuipingL/WanderDream GitHub address as the intended code-and-data release location; v1 only promises release. Implementation details and appendix prompts are unchanged, and the PDFs do not establish that release has occurred.

R1.justification: The same 134 references and related-work discussion are retained. Positioning relative to existing situated-reasoning datasets and world-model approaches is unchanged.

P1.justification: The corresponding-author designation changes from Junwei Zheng to Kailun Yang, and the first-page footnote adds contact emails. Apart from the release-address addition, the narrative wording and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 uses larger pages with wider margins and reflows the opening pages. Figure 2 moves from page 2 to 3 and Figure 4 from page 6 to 7; figure artwork, captions, and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added repository destination and author contact emails modestly improve access guidance. Scientific content, supporting evidence, and appendices remain unchanged; both versions still describe code and data release as forthcoming.
